To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a selectivity correction is necessary when estimating a second step model of the type suggested here, (b) the correction terms depend upon multivariate normal integrations that cannot be easily computed, (c) the integrals may be replaced by simulators and (d) the simulators can be used both for the choice probabilities and for conditional moments

(i) two step estimation is a viable alternative to full information for the estimation of discrete/ continuous econometric models, and (ii) in situations involving interdependent multinomial choices, selectivity correction terms can be used in a regression based estimation procedure, and the resulting estimator can be implemented using efficient simulators.

1) the two step estimation procedure is a valid alternative to the full information one; 2) the two step approach can be implemented with a regression based specification and 3) the correction terms can be computed efficiently using simulation techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of a discrete/continuous model where the discrete part is described with an interdependent multinomial choice model.
the development of a two step procedure for the estimation of discrete/ continuous models with interdependent choices.
two step estimation of interdependent multinomial probit discrete/continuous econometrics models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology is a valuable tool for the estimation of discrete/continous econometric models.
the proposed method is a very promising approach for dealing with interdependent discrete/continuous econometrics models.
the technique suggested is a very useful and practical alternative to the full information approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an estimation technique that is simple and efficient for the estimation of discrete/ continuous econometric models with interdependent multinomial choices.
we have developed a computationally tractable procedure to estimate a class of models that have been difficult to handle in the past.
the two step approach with selectivity correction terms provides a simple and efficient way to deal with discrete/continuous interrelated choices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the two step procedure with selectivity corrections is a viable alternative to a full information one when the choices are interdependent.
the use of selectivity correction terms in a two step procedure is a viable approach for the estimation of interdependent discrete/continuous models.
a simple two step estimator can be used to model complex discrete/continuous econometrics problems with interdependent choices.
